Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly as an AI player.

I have $59 and four mortgaged properties. The opponent has $1,939 and a strong orange and light blue set. I need to decide whether to trade or mortgage.

p2 rejected a $200 offer for Pennsylvania Avenue. I cannot mortgage Ventnor now. Rolling 8 lands on Penn RR for $200. Rolls 9 through 12 hit orange hotels for $950. I will end the turn.

Trading with p1 would let them complete greens and build hotels, which would be dangerous. I will not sell my yellows. Mortgaging Ventnor would give me $130 and bring my cash to $189.

Mortgaging Ventnor still leaves me $11 short of the $200 Penn RR fee. I would go bankrupt on that space even after mortgaging.

I checked the mortgage value and confirmed it is $130. I am now considering whether p2 would accept a smaller trade offer, since they previously rejected $200 for the property.

A yellow monopoly is impossible with only $59. I am now considering selling a property to p1 to raise cash, since they need North Carolina and Pennsylvania to complete their greens.

p1 already owns the dark blue monopoly, but Park Place is mortgaged so they cannot build there yet. They still hold orange hotels, which are the most dangerous set. Pennsylvania Avenue alone would not complete their greens because North Carolina is unowned. I am reconsidering whether to sell it to p1, since they need it to finish their green set.

I will propose selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p1 for $200–400. That would cover the Penn RR rent and give me a cushion.

I am second-guessing the trade plan. My prior strategy was to end the turn if p2 refused, and p2 just did. I am now reconsidering whether that is still optimal. I am also mapping the spaces from Reading Railroad.

I mapped the spaces from Reading Railroad. St. Charles, States, and Virginia belong to p1 but form no monopoly. The next danger is the Pennsylvania Railroad at $200. St. James and Tennessee are orange hotels at $950 each. I am now recounting the exact dice sums that land on these spaces.

I mapped the exact dice sums from Reading Railroad. Rolls 10 and 12 land on orange hotels for $950 each, while roll 9 hits Penn RR for $200. I also noted that New York is unreachable in one roll, and that a Chance card could force an even worse outcome.

I need at least $11 more cash before the roll to survive the Penn RR rent. I will trade for that amount, ideally around $150, since mortgaging Ventnor now still leaves me short. p2 previously rejected $200 and $125, but they now have $714 after buying Illinois for $240.

I traced the recent turns to confirm p2 has $714. They previously rejected $200 because they needed cash for orange hotels, so a lower offer of $100–125 might succeed. Receiving $125 would bring my cash to $184, which still leaves me $16 short of the $200 Penn RR fee unless I mortgage Ventnor.

I realized that even a $50 trade would cover the Penn RR rent if I mortgage Ventnor, since $59 plus $50 plus $130 equals $189. But mortgaging Ventnor means losing my only rent income. I am now checking whether mortgaged properties still count toward monopolies.

I confirmed that Ventnor rent is only $22, so mortgaging it is not a major loss. I also noted that the mortgage value is $130 but unmortgaging costs $143. Selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p2 for $125 would cover the Penn RR rent and leave me with $184, though I would still be unable to survive the orange hotels. I am now weighing whether the green blocker is worth keeping, since p1 still needs North Carolina to complete their greens.

Selling to p2 is preferable to selling to p1. I will try offering $75–100 for Pennsylvania Avenue, framing it as cheap insurance against the orange hotels.

I am now considering p1 as a buyer. They have plenty of cash and could pay $400–500 for Pennsylvania Avenue, but that would not cover the $297 needed to unmortgage my yellows or build hotels. I also worry that p1 might buy North Carolina next, completing their green set and becoming even more dangerous.

I calculated that three houses on all three yellows would cost roughly $1,650, which is impossible with only $59. I will not trade my yellows for a developed set because I have no cash to build. I will offer p2 $100 for Pennsylvania Avenue.

I am now considering p1 as a buyer. They have $1,939 and would pay roughly $150–250 for a mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue, since North Carolina is still unowned and they want my deeds. Selling to them would give me $309 in cash, which would cover the Penn RR rent without needing to mortgage Ventnor.

Selling to p1 for $309 would leave only $12 after unmortgaging both yellows, so it is not enough to build or survive. I need roughly $450 to unmortgage the yellows and keep a $200 cushion. No opponent is likely to pay that much for a mortgaged property.

I will propose a trade now. I am weighing p2 at $100 against p1 at $300–400, since ending the turn is certain death.

I realized p2 would profit more from my bankruptcy than from any trade. If I survive their railroad rent, they collect my properties. They rejected the $200 offer because it would have let me pay their rent and avoid their property collection. A $100 trade would look desperate and still leave them with a clear advantage.

I will not waste a trade on p2. They prefer my bankruptcy so they can claim all my properties.

p1 has no incentive to help me survive. If I live, I will eventually land on their orange hotels and die. They want my yellows when that happens.

I realized p1 has an incentive to help me survive. If I die on Penn RR, p2 collects my yellows. Keeping me alive through the railroads lets me die on p1's orange hotels instead, which means p1 gets my properties. I will offer p1 $200 for mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue so I can survive the railroad rent and avoid giving p2 my yellows.

I will ask p1 for $250–300 for mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. That would cover the Penn RR rent and leave me with about $109. I still cannot pay the orange hotel rent of $950, so I would die to the oranges regardless. If I land on p2 first, they would collect my yellows. If I land on p1 first, they would collect them instead. The trade only delays the inevitable bankruptcy.

I will ask p1 for $300 for mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. That covers the Penn RR rent and leaves a small cushion, so I do not need to mortgage Ventnor. If they counter lower, I can negotiate.

I will offer mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue to p1 for $250. That covers the Penn RR rent and leaves me with about $59, so I do not need to mortgage Ventnor. I will frame the trade as a strategic move to keep my yellows out of their hands rather than as a desperate request.

I will ask p1 for $300 for mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. I rejected a higher anchor of $400 because it would invite a low counter, and I need cash rather than more mortgaged properties.

I raised the trade anchor to $350. I will frame it as mortgaged green for $176 to unmortgage, with the net cost high but the strategic value of keeping my yellows out of p2's hands.

I will ask p1 for $250 for mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. I realized they already own Boardwalk and could unmortgage Park Place to build dark blues, so they may not need the green deed itself. The real hook is keeping my yellows out of gpt's hands.
